intro: Delaware runs its elections through the state Department of Elections and its three county offices in New Castle, Kent and Sussex.

id_rule.text: You do not have to show ID, but poll workers will ask for it. Showing a Delaware driver's license or state ID, a U.S. passport, or a similar document with your photo or signature makes check-in faster. If you do not show ID, you fill out a form before you vote.

dates.label: Last day to register to vote
dates.detail: The deadline for unregistered citizens is 11:59 pm on this date. Uniformed service members and citizens living overseas have until Oct. 19.

dates.label: Early voting
dates.detail: Vote at an early voting site in your county. Hours differ by day, and there is no early voting on Sunday, Oct. 25.

dates.label: Last day to get a mail ballot from your county office
dates.detail: County Department of Elections offices can issue absentee ballots until noon on this day. The quickest way to request one is the iVote portal.

dates.label: Election Day
dates.detail: Polls are open 7 am to 8 pm. A mail ballot must reach your county Department of Elections office by 8 pm.
